D R A P E R C I T Y
Parks, Recreation & Trails Master Plan

1. Overall satisfaction with Draper parks and recreation facilities is high
• Draper residents are highly satisfied with the provision of parks and rec facilities, with well over 80% of respondents saying they are
satisfied. Respondents who are very physically active are more likely to say they are satisfied with parks and rec opportunities in the City.
2. Respondents use Draper trails and parks/facilities often, and they like having them close by
• A majority of respondents, 55%, say they use Draper parks (or fields and rec facilities) a few times a month or more, and, cumulatively,
around 70% respondents are using Draper parks at least once a month. Additionally, over 70% of respondents say having parks close to
them is important.
• Nearly 2/3 of respondents, 63%, say they use trails a few times a month or more, and, cumulatively, about 3/4 of respondents are using
trails at least once a month. Most respondents, about 2/3, spent between 1 and 2 hours on trails when they use them.
3. Nearly all respondents say they are satisfied with arts and cultural events in Draper
• Nearly 80% of respondents say Draper provides an adequate amount of arts and cultural events, and respondents particularly enjoy the
Draper Days events. Respondents are interested in Draper City offering more concerts.
4. Preserving natural space and improving recreational facilities has broad support among respondents
• In terms of future development projects, purchasing and preserving more natural open space is the potential priority area that has the
most support (around 1 in 5 respondents allocate some portion of their hypothetical budget to this initiative).
5. Most residents are willing to support parks and recreation funding measures
• On average, respondents would be willing to pay $64 more per year in property taxes to fund parks and rec development and operation.
Additionally, 77% of respondents are at least somewhat willing to pay a nominal annual usage fee to fund park maintenance and
upgrades.

CITY PARKS, TRAILS MOST IMPORTANT FACILITIES

By far, Draper City parks and trails are seen as most important to residents, with72%having marked it as in their top 3 most important facilities.Public lands fall close
behind in terms of importance, followed by churches and school programs. Only 2% of residents indicate that their recreational needs are not being met.
TRAILS, POOLS, PLAYGROUNDS MOST UTILIZED

When asked their physical activity, 54% of respondents say they are ”very” or “somewhat” active.The Draper City recreational facilities most utilized by respondents is
trails, with 67% of respondents having used paved trails during the past year and 57% having used natural surface trails. Pools and playgrounds are also quite popular.

as you please, but the total must be $100.

The vast majority (70%) of Draper residents use Draper City parks, trails, and recreation facilities at least once a month. An even larger majority (93%) consider it at least
somewhat important to have a public park within walking distance of their home.

Being close to home is by far the most important reason that Draper residents frequent their most used park. Using the trails/jogging paths is a less common, albeit
significant reason. When it comes to improving their most frequented park, a plurality of respondents (14%) say that no improvements are needed. Among those who do see
a need for improvement, the most common requests made include constructing pickleball courts, enhancing maintenance and atmosphere, and improving lighting.

Residents are divided about whether dogs and their owners cause conflicts in parks and trails. Among those who express concern, nearly half prefer to resolve conflicts by
increasing enforcement/fines . Just under a third say they prefer to create more off-leash dog areas and dedicated dog parks.
MOST RESIDENTS USE TRAILS REGULARLY

The majority (63%) of Draper residents use City trails a few times a month or more. Only 5% never use or visit City trails. Among those who do use City trails, the vast
majority of residents spend 1-2 hours on the trails per visit, and only 12% typically spend less than per visit.

DRAPER CITY PAVED TRAILS MOST VISITED TRAILS

Draper City Paved Trails is by far the most visited trail system in Draper City, utilized by 60% of residents. Corner Canyon Multi-use Trails are also quite popular. By
comparison, the MehrabanWetlands Trails are the least popular of the City trails, utilized by only 6% of residents.

RESIDENTS PREFER TRAILS THAT ARE CLOSE TO HOME

A plurality of Draper residents use their favorite trail because it is close to home. Another significant proportion of residents use their favorite trail for recreational biking
and walking/jogging. In terms of improving Draper trails, residents most commonly want more dog trails, restrooms, and paved trails.

RESIDENTS WANT MORE PAVED & MULTI-USE TRAILS

Residents are generally satisfied with the number of natural surface, one-way bike trails in the City and express the greatest interest in increasing the number of paved
trails and natural surface multi-use trails in the City. Residents also express interest in having trails designated for specifically hikers rather than sharing trails with bikers.

RESIDENTS WOULD USE INDOOR TRACK, GYMNASIUM

When asked about indoor facilities they or members of their household would use, a plurality of Draper residents express interest in using an indoor running/walking track.
An almost equal proportion say they would make use of a multi-purpose gymnasium. Few individuals express interest in using an indoor turf field or game room.

FACILITIES, OPEN SPACE, OR TRAILS BOND TO RECEIVE MOST SUPPORT

Nearly a third (30%) of Draper residents suggest they would be more likely to support a bond for recreational facilities thanany other potential amenity or funding
category, though 18% indicate that would be their last choice. In terms of total support, funding for open space, trails, andparks are all popular options while funding for
arts and cultural programs is much less popular. Forty-two percent of residents say they would be least likely to support a bondfor funding arts and cultural programs.
